We are a diverse and lively school at the heart of Oxford’s Cowley Road. We take a pride in knowing children as unique individuals, and have a hardworking and dedicated staff team who are committed to enabling all to succeed.
Alongside rigorously planned programmes in Literacy and Numeracy, we offer an exciting curriculum which is enriched by high-quality provision, particularly in the creative arts. We ensure that children in our school are valued and listened to, and place a strong emphasis on the development of social skills and self-esteem.
We are a truly international school, with over 40 languages spoken and extensive experience in supporting new arrivals to the UK. Our results at the end of KS2 have been significantly above national and Oxford averages for the last two years (78%).
Childhood is a very special time, and we are committed to making it as happy and productive as possible for all of the children in our care.
Russell Kaye, Headteacher

Expert Curriculum
At East Oxford Primary School, we have developed an "expert" curriculum which enables children to study and research themes in depth which generate high levels of interest and motivation. Our curriculum is unique in that the topic blocks have been developed by a working party of children in partnership with staff. We fulfil (and go beyond!) the orders for the revised National Curriculum. We also work in partnership with external organisations such as Quest for Learning and Oxfordshire Music Service to enhance our curriculum.
Strong attention is given to ensuring that all our children make rapid progress in basic skills and apply these throughout their learning. Last year, children across the school made progress which was significantly better than that typically found nationally.
Early Years Foundation Stage. The core feature of our curriculum in the Foundation Stage is the close attention and detail paid to a strong child initiated and reactive curriculum. Regular parental Stay and Play sessions with personalised learning planning ensures that all children get off to a flying start at East Oxford. Our setting has a superb outdoor environment where children can access daily learning activities mirroring our indoor provision.
KS1 The curriculum is based on a balance of formal teaching and close attention to each child's development in social skills, creativity, and understanding of the world. We have highly structured programmes in place for phonics and mathematics, as well as a dedicated support teacher and team of teaching assistants who deliver intervention where it is required. Children are grouped in single and mixed-age classes, but are always taught according to their individual needs. Learning at this age is practical, fun and creative and takes account of children's developing individual needs. We use Bug Club Phonics to develop early reading skills.
KS2 As children move to KS2, they learn to apply their skills to increasingly complex tasks through a variety of learning opportunities, including specific teaching in literacy and mathematics. We also introduce the teaching of Italian across KS2.
PSHE&C. We place a strong emphasis on PSHE&C and use the PSHE&C Association scheme of work. This supports our children in developing effective learning behaviours, emotional literacy, and understanding their place as citizens within the wider community. Click here to find out how we promote British values through our curriculum.
Please take time to read the documents on the right, which outline how we intend to deliver the National Curriculum over the coming year and what the key expectations are for each age group. Documents will be added here as they are completed.
Parents have a statutory right to withdraw their children from part of all of the RE curriculum. They should book a meeting with the headteacher if they wish to discuss this. If you wish to find out more about our curriculum, please request this information from the school office.

pageCache.text:
Performing Arts
At East Oxford, we place a high priority on the Performing Arts, including Music, Drama and Dance.
We do this because we believe that this gives children a confidence which they can then apply to different areas of their learning, as well as developing their speaking and listening skills.
All of our children learn to play a brass instrument in Years 4 & 5, and our children have sung everywhere from the local Tesco to the Sheldonian.
We have dance clubs, a street dance squad, and enter national competitions each year.
Every year, our Year 6s hire out a local theatre, and stage a high quality musical production, which recently have included "Into the Woods", "Honk!" and "Annie."

Our Governors
The school has a governing body, which has a wide range of duties and responsibilities.
Governing bodies are made up of representatives from the Local Authority, the school staff, parents and the local community. Our governing body meets in full once a term to consider the work of the school and to check that it is on track to meet the children's needs. Much of the work of the Governing Body is delegated to smaller committees, which meet regularly.
The full governing body meets 4 times per annum, and three committees (Standards & Curriculum, Resources, and Community) meet once each long term. A pay committee meets annually.
Our governors are very supportive and interested in the welfare and education of the children. They are kept fully informed of all aspects of school life, including the curriculum. They are also involved in the appointment of staff to the school. From time to time, elections are held for parent representatives.
The day-to-day leadership of the school rests with the Headteacher, who should usually be your first point of call for any queries or concerns you may have. Should you wish to make a complaint about the school, please see the relevant policy on the complaints page. Governors can be contacted via the school office.

Music Development Plan
At East Oxford, we place a strong value on the performing arts and Music. Our children sing on a weekly basis, and have performed everywhere from the Cowley Road Tesco to the Sheldonian. We follow Charanga as a music scheme with weekly lessons in class. Children in Years 4 & 5 all learn a brass instrument as part of our music curriculum with Oxfordshire Music Service.
Find out more in our Music Development Plan.
